max_tire.note: Listed by 6061 Works as a mild upgrade, about 15 mm taller than stock. We couldn't verify an owner consensus for anything bigger.
Nissan Australia and Premcar's factory-backed combination, with re-valved HBMC.
6061 Works' recommendation after a 2-in lift; offsets of +18 to +25 mm suit wider tyres.
Nissan sells front and rear crown-wheel-and-pinion sets for Y62s on 35s (Patrolapart).

items.title: Rear-view camera image can be turned off
items.summary: Camera display settings could hide the rear-view image, failing FMVSS 111. Dealers updated the software.

items.title: Fuel pump impeller can swell and bind
items.summary: The fuel pump can fail and stall the engine. Dealers replace the fuel pump module (Nissan R21A2).

items.title: Incorrect axle weight rating on certification label
items.summary: The label's gross axle weight rating is wrong, which could lead to overloading. Dealers fit new labels.

timeline.change: Y62 launched in Abu Dhabi on 13 February and on sale in the UAE from 1 April; Infiniti QX56 (Z62) brings the platform to North America
Early trucks: CarSwitch flags transmission valve-body issues and early fit-and-finish problems
First facelift (June): revised tail lights and LED headlights
CarSwitch's value sweet spot for used Y62s: it says most early-production mechanical kinks had been sorted by then
Second-generation Armada (Y62) on sale in the US in August as a 2017 model; Series 3 Patrols get an electronic thermostat from February
VQ40DE V6 for entry Middle East grades; seven-speed automatic standard across the range
Second Patrol facelift with a new front end and Nissan Intelligent Mobility driver aids. CarSwitch and Westside Auto rate these 2020-on facelift Patrols as the most desirable used Y62s
Armada refresh (on sale January): new nose, 400 hp, premium fuel per EPA; Middle East 70th Anniversary edition in December
Patrol Warrior by Premcar in Australia: 50 mm lift, 295/70R18 tyres, re-valved HBMC
Y63 unveiled in Abu Dhabi (3 September); third-generation Armada on sale in the US in December

identify.intro: Patrols, Armadas, Nismos, Warriors and the Infiniti QX56/QX80 share a body and engine but differ in what they can do off-road. Check what's actually fitted.

items.head: Armada vs Patrol
items.body: A US Armada has no locking differentials, no disconnecting sway bars and no HBMC (AutoGuide).

items.head: HBMC or not
items.body: HBMC trucks have hydraulic lines running to each damper. The Desert Edition used regular suspension (Wikipedia), and so did every Armada.

items.head: Series and parts
items.body: Parts change by series. Patrolapart lists different thermostats for Series 1–2 and Series 3-on trucks (from February 2016) and two different timing chains for some 2016–2017 Series 3 trucks. Give your parts supplier the VIN.

items.head: Warrior
items.body: Premcar's 2023 Warrior has 323 mm of ground clearance, 295/70R18 Yokohama all-terrains, a 2.5 mm steel front bash plate and a 3,620 kg GVM (4X4 Australia).

items.head: Nismo
items.body: The Gulf-market Nismo has a 319 kW (428 hp) V8, Bilstein dampers and 22-inch forged wheels (Wikipedia).

values.intro: The Y62 holds value best in the Gulf, where it's a cultural icon. We couldn't find a reliable published price guide for the US Armada, so these figures are UAE estimates.
values.note: CarSwitch's mid-2026 UAE estimates. Nismos run AED 140k–200k (2016–2019) and AED 230k+ (2020 on). Bring a Trailer has no Y62 or Armada sales to compare.

paragraphs: The Y62 Patrol was never sold in the US. Its US version is the 2017–2024 Nissan Armada (and the Infiniti QX56/QX80). NHTSA's 25-year exemption counts from the date of manufacture, so the earliest 2010 Patrols become eligible around 2035, and a non-US Patrol can't be imported before then unless it meets US standards.
Japan is the reverse case: Wikipedia says the Y62 was export-only there, and most Y62s registered in Japan are reverse-imported left-hand-drive US Armadas.

production.intro: Nissan Shatai built the Y62 in Japan for export markets. Japan itself never got it new.
